solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Learned Irishman travelling west, damned without St John

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading right to left, so the letters run backwards
'without' here means lacking, so some letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: the damned are lost souls
the usual abbreviation for saint, removed from the previous word
john is slang for a toilet, as is lav

explanation.surface: An educated Irishman heading west in disgrace, with no saint to help him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like the saint's name continuing 'St John', but the saint is only the abbreviation to remove; John alone is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An ollav was a master scholar or poet of ancient Ireland, a title for a learned man of rank.

clue.text: Snowflake periodically baleful, upsetting group of old fossils

indicators.note: something done periodically recurs at fixed intervals, so only letters at regular spacing are kept

parts.note: every third letter: the 3rd, 6th and 9th

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting tips the word over so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: baleful and sullen both describe a gloomy, menacing look

explanation.surface: A sensitive soul, now and then glowering, upsets a group of old fogeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old fossils' looks like slang for elderly people, but the definition is literal. Only SULLEN is reversed; the letters from 'Snowflake' are taken every third place.
explanation.definitionFit: Olenellus is a genus of Cambrian trilobites, extinct marine arthropods known only from rock specimens.

clue.text: Like a phalarope — shy, mottled, with head slightly dipped

indicators.note: dipping the head a little lowers the leading letter just one place, so the word's order shifts slightly

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to lob
pied means patched in two colours, like a magpie

explanation.surface: A wading bird described as timid, speckled and ducking its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid but is the verb to throw. In PIED the first letter moves down one place, giving IPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Phalaropes have lobed toes for swimming, and lobiped means having lobed feet, so it describes the bird.

clue.text: Seaweed containing iodine, mostly cut up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read from the bottom upwards
to contain is to hold inside, so one piece goes within another
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to cut meat is to carve it
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Kelp that is rich in iodine, chopped almost to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: CARVE loses its last letter and is reversed to VRAC, which then holds the I. 'Cut up' looks like a single phrase but splits into the word and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vraic is the Channel Islands name for seaweed gathered from the shore and used as fertiliser or fuel.

clue.text: British single about embracing semi-uneasy charms

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one part wraps around another

parts.note: a standard abbreviation for British

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word faces the other way

parts.note: sole means one and only

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the next word is kept

parts.note: queasy means uneasy or unsettled

explanation.surface: A British record that wraps itself round songs that half-unsettle and charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like a pop record, but it means one and only; 'about' turns that word round rather than meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Breloques are small ornaments hung from a watch chain, trinkets also called charms.

clue.text: Flower in channel adjacent to pollarded tree

indicators.note: pollarding cuts the top growth off, so the head letter of the word is removed

parts.note: the Beeb is a nickname for the BBC, the British broadcaster
the palm is a tree; it loses its top
placed next to, so the pieces simply join

explanation.surface: A flower growing in a ditch next to a cut-back tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like a watercourse but is a TV channel: the Beeb is the British nickname for the BBC. PALM minus its top gives ALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bee balm, or bergamot, is a North American plant of the mint family grown for its scarlet blossoms.

clue.text: See island immersed in total state of delight

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: something immersed sits inside a liquid, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a total is a sum
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Picture an island steeped in pure bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' reads as the verb to look, but it is a bishop's see; Ely is an English cathedral city in the fens.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium was the Greek paradise for heroes, and by extension any condition of perfect happiness.

clue.text: Little wood pigeon's half worried with hawks beginning to attack

indicators.note: half means only one of two equal parts is kept
something worried is fretted and shaken about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the back half of the bird's name
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A small pigeon fretting as hawks begin their attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little wood pigeon' wants to be one phrase, a small wood pigeon; in fact 'Little wood' is the definition and 'pigeon's half' supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oakenshaw is a small oak wood; shaw is an old word for a thicket or copse.

clue.text: Let me see both sides of beaver before Edmund's visor

parts.note: um is the noise of someone pausing to think

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the animal
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone pauses over a beaver and a mysterious Edmund's visor.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund is Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene. A beaver is also part of a helmet, which nudges toward armour, but here it just supplies its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbrere is Spenser's spelling of umbrere or umbriere, the movable face guard on a helmet that shades the eyes.

clue.text: Exhausted sheep and deer shiver up north

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied, so the inside letters are gone and only the outer ones remain

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle
the elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: Tired sheep and deer shivering in the cold of the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiver' looks like trembling with cold, but here it is a noun meaning a splinter; 'up north' marks a northern English dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelk is a northern dialect noun for a splinter or sliver of wood, which a shiver also means.

clue.text: Abrasive retrospective energy provider probes corruption of jury

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: emery is a gritty abrasive powder

indicators.note: a retrospective looks backwards, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: a carb (carbohydrate) is a food that supplies energy

explanation.surface: A scratchy retrospective by a power company investigates jury tampering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy provider' suggests a utility company, but it is a food that fuels the body, a carbohydrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Embracery is the legal offence of trying to influence a juror by bribes or threats.

clue.text: Back in dock, bishop entering affray exposed churchman once

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece goes within another
exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed
the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word
an affray is a brawl, a melee
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop dragged into a brawl and exposed, back in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: MELEE stripped of its outer letters gives ELE, into which B goes; 'dock' sounds like a courtroom but just gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keble was a nineteenth-century Anglican priest and poet, a leader of the Oxford Movement, so a cleric of the past.

clue.text: When spirit is due, bar swapping case of cheap bottled wine with tea, OK

indicators.note: bottled is slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger into a new order
to swap is to exchange places, so two letters trade positions

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except

indicators.note: a case is the outside covering, so only the outer letters are meant

parts.note: the outside letters of the word; these two trade places
taken as written

explanation.surface: At the pub, someone trades a case of cheap wine for tea instead, and that's fine.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXCEPT the C and P swap places to make EXPECT. 'Bottled' looks like it describes the wine, but it is the anagram signal, slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectation Week is the church name for the days between Ascension and Whitsun, when the disciples awaited the Holy Spirit.

clue.text: Resin, the first university's extracted from opiate

indicators.note: to extract is to pull out, so letters are removed from the word

parts.note: laudanum is a tincture of opium
U is the abbreviation for university; only its first occurrence goes

explanation.surface: A resin forms after a university has extracted it from an opium drug.
explanation.walkthrough: LAUDANUM has two Us; 'the first' says only the earlier one is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladanum (labdanum) is a sticky gum exuded by rockrose shrubs and used in perfumery.

clue.text: US finance hub introducing trade agreement primarily cuts off one with diminished vision

parts.note: New York City, home of Wall Street

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the first letters of the two words
to lop is to cut off
placed in front of what follows

explanation.surface: Wall Street launching a trade deal that cuts someone short-sighted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts off' looks like a deletion signal but is plain wordplay for LOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nyctalops is a person with night blindness (or, in older use, day blindness), so their sight is impaired.

clue.text: I now understand male prophet catches fish

indicators.note: to catch is to hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
a seer foresees the future
ah is the exclamation of sudden realisation

explanation.surface: Someone realises a male prophet is catching fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation goes between M and SEER, held inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The mahseer is a large freshwater game fish of South Asian rivers, related to carp.

clue.text: Little fliers notary distributed about church hospital charges

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
to charge is to rush in, so one piece enters another
distributed things are scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A notary hands out leaflets about church hospital fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little fliers' suggests leaflets but means insects. The shuffled notary goes round CH, then H charges into the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhynchota is an old name for the Hemiptera, the true bugs, many of which are small winged insects.

clue.text: Might they drop round in Caledonian coastal waters?

definitions.text: Might they drop round in Caledonian coastal waters?

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so a letter is lost

parts.note: sea lochs are Scottish inlets; Caledonian means Scottish
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Do these creatures pop in for a visit in Scottish coastal inlets?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop round' reads as visiting, but it means drop O; the whole clue also describes seals turning up in sea lochs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealch is the Scots word for a seal, the marine mammal common in the inlets of the Scottish coast.

clue.text: Mineral rights initially squandered throughout separate ceremony

indicators.note: squandered means wasted away, and throughout says it happens in every piece

parts.note: apart means separate
a rite is a ritual ceremony

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Mining rights were wasted all through a divorce ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes from both words: APART becomes APAT and RITE becomes ITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Apatite is a common phosphate mineral found in rocks, teeth and bones.

clue.text: Boer pedlar's small, effective kitty

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a cat that is good at catching mice

explanation.surface: A South African hawker's cat is small but a good hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' could suggest a pool of money, but it is a cat, and an effective one is a mouser.
explanation.definitionFit: Smouser is South African slang for an itinerant trader or hawker, from the Dutch.

clue.text: Ivy barely turning yellow, as is sequoia

indicators.note: turning things move about, so the letters are rearranged
barely means stripped bare, so the outer letters go and only the middle remains

parts.note: the plant's name stripped of its outside letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ivy hardly yellowing, just like a giant redwood.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as botany, but sequoia is cited as a word: it contains all five vowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequoia has five vowels and only two consonants, so it is rich in vowels, which is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Film involves new network site that Norsemen visited

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: vid is short for video, a film
N is the abbreviation for new
a local area network

explanation.surface: A documentary features a new network at a Viking landing site.
explanation.walkthrough: Vid is informal shorthand for a video, and a LAN is a local area network of computers.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinland is the Norse name for the part of North America reached by Leif Erikson around 1000 AD.

clue.text: Shot rang out, echo pervading large lake

indicators.note: to pervade is to spread right through, so the pieces sit within another

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large
L is the abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Echo is E in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A gunshot rang out, its echo carrying across a big lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a verb but is the noun, the definition. The rearranged letters plus E fill the space between two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Langrel, or langrage, is case shot of iron scraps fired from a cannon to tear an enemy's rigging.

clue.text: Possibly not a coma, nothing close to death

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many that might be made, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; all fifteen letters are used

explanation.surface: Maybe it isn't a coma at all, nothing like being on the brink of dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coma' and 'close to death' sit together naturally, but the coma is only letters; all fifteen of the first four words are rearranged, with 'Possibly' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanatognomonic is a medical term for a symptom indicating that a patient is about to die.

clue.text: Crown taken off royal family tree

indicators.note: removing the crown takes off the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the Stuarts were a royal house of Scotland and England

explanation.surface: The crown is stripped from a royal dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' suggests a monarch's headgear, apt for royalty, but it means the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuart is a Western Australian eucalyptus prized for its hard, durable timber.

clue.text: Ace pop duo served up alcohol

definitions.note: mahwa is the tree whose flowers are distilled into a spirit; the definition names the drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means sent upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
Wham! were George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley

explanation.surface: A brilliant pop pair dished out drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' looks like a waiter's job, but it signals a reversal in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahwa, or mahua, is an Indian tree whose sweet flowers are fermented and distilled into a liquor of the same name.

clue.text: Former dispatch boat is to put in river shortly

indicators.note: putting something in means placing it inside another piece
shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the Avon is an English river
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old dispatch boat is about to be launched on a river soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' reads as 'soon' but means the river's name loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviso was a fast naval vessel once used to carry messages and orders between ships.

clue.text: Hit Victorian dandy into endless smut

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, sitting inside it
endless means without an end, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: smut is a flake of soot
a masher was a Victorian fop who pestered women

explanation.surface: Punching a Victorian toff into an unending pile of filth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smut' suggests obscenity, but here it is the older sense, a flake of soot. A masher was a Victorian ladies' man.
explanation.definitionFit: A smasheroo is slang for a huge success, the same sense as a hit show or song.

clue.text: Very confident daughter displaying subordinary signs

parts.note: très is French for very
sure means confident
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A self-assured daughter shows signs of inferiority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subordinary' reads like 'subordinate', but a subordinary is a heraldic charge; the tressure is a thin inner border on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is tressured when it bears a tressure, one of the minor heraldic charges called subordinaries.

clue.text: At last, tea urn sent round Clackmannanshire town

indicators.note: sending something round turns it to face the other way
at last points to the very end of a word, its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the drink
an olla is an earthenware pot or urn

explanation.surface: Finally the tea urn is passed around a small Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' looks like 'finally', but it takes the last letter of the following word. Clackmannanshire is a small county in central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is the main town of Clackmannanshire, on the north bank of the Forth in Scotland.
